edge.title: The police do not hold you on video
edge.setup: A call: a parcel in your name held at Mumbai customs, contents illegal. Transferred to a 'CBI officer' in uniform on video, a station behind him, a case number, your real PAN read back. You are told it's a sealed probe — tell no one, stay on camera, and 'verify' your funds in a government escrow account while they clear your name.
edge.tell: Any demand to stay on the line, stay on camera, or tell nobody is the attack itself.
move: Hang up. Nothing lawful ever requires your continuous presence on a video call.
Call 1930 (cyber-fraud) or report at cybercrime.gov.in from a different phone.
Tell one family member immediately — isolation is the only thing making this work.
edge.why: There is no such thing as a digital arrest in Indian law. Police act with physical summons and paperwork. The entire scam is an isolation engine: uniform supplies authority, secrecy removes anyone who'd say 'that isn't a thing', and the clock removes your ability to check.
edge.variants: Same shape: 'your SIM is being used in a crime', fake TRAI disconnection calls, 'your son is in custody' ransom calls.

lens.name: Compounding
lens.one_line: Small consistent changes beat big sporadic ones, because the result is multiplicative, not additive.
lens.detail: Intuition is linear; compounding isn't, which is why almost everyone underestimates it. ₹5,000 a month at 12% is about ₹11 lakh in 10 years and roughly ₹50 lakh in 20 — most of that gain arriving in the final stretch. The same shape governs skills, reputation and debt. Credit-card interest at 3.5% a month is this force running against you at roughly 50% a year.
elsewhere: Minimum card payments keeping a balance alive for years.
Reputation: slow to build, then suddenly everything arrives at once.
lens.test: Is this a one-time event, or something that multiplies? Multiplying things deserve disproportionate attention.
lens.today: Moneycontrol reports that on a ₹12 lakh salary, Bengaluru traffic can cost nearly ₹1 lakh a year in lost time. Each daily delay looks trivial, but it repeats every working day and the loss accumulates. The same logic is behind the Biocon story (TOI): over 1,500 employees have moved from private to public transport, a small daily change that compounds in the other direction.

carry_over.prompt: Your hospital package quote has grown by discharge and you are asked to settle while someone is still in a bed. What is the tell?
carry_over.answer: You're being asked to agree to money at the exact moment you are least able to walk away.
